applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: France-China Agreement on the Promotion and Reciprocal Protection of Investments, signed 2007 and in force
France-China Convention for the Avoidance of Double Taxation and the Prevention of Fiscal Evasion with Respect to Taxes on Income, signed 2013 and in force
France-European Union treaty framework and directly applicable EU corporate, AML, sanctions, consumer, customs, and digital-commerce legislation

EU trade agreements applicable to France, including the EU-UK Trade and Cooperation Agreement and other agreements in force for the relevant origin and destination markets

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Primary AML/CFT framework: French Monetary and Financial Code (Code monétaire et financier), Articles L.561-1 through L.561-50 and related regulatory provisions, implementing EU Directive (EU) 2015/849 as amended. Beneficial-owner definition: Articles L.561-2-2, R.561-1, R.561-2 and R.561-3 of the Monetary and Financial Code. Beneficial-owner filing obligation for commercial companies: French Commercial Code, Articles L.561-46 through L.561-50, as amended by Law No. 2016-1691 of 9 December 2016 and subsequent AML legislation. Implementing beneficial-owner filing rules include Decree No. 2017-1094 of 12 June 2017 and Decree No. 2018-284 of 18 April 2018. The beneficial-owner register is maintained through the French business register system and is subject to restricted-access rules introduced under the transposition of the Court of Justice of the European Union judgment in Joined Cases C-37/20 and C-601/20.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Passport or national identity document of each shareholder, director, legal representative, and identified beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent passport or identity-document authority in the country of nationality
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille OR Consular Legalization, if a certified copy is required and the issuing country is not covered by an applicable exemption

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of incorporation, certificate of good standing, or current commercial-register extract of each corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Commercial or corporate registry in the country of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille OR Consular Legalization, followed by a certified French translation where required

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified constitutional documents and current articles of association of each corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate registry, notary, or competent corporate-records authority in the country of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille OR Consular Legalization, unless an applicable treaty or registry-verification mechanism removes the requirement

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Corporate authorization approving the French investment, incorporation, share subscription, and appointment of the representative
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board, shareholder, or other competent governing body of the corporate investor
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization or certified corporate signature, followed by Hague Apostille OR Consular Legalization where executed abroad

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Ownership chart and beneficial-owner declaration identifying every natural person who directly or indirectly owns more than 25 percent or exercises control by other means
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate investor and ultimate beneficial owners; supporting registry documents issued by relevant corporate registries
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Certified signature and supporting public-document authentication by Hague Apostille OR Consular Legalization where required

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of residential address for each beneficial owner and controlling officer
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility provider, bank, governmental authority, or other accepted address-document issuer in the relevant country
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Normally no apostille for a recent private document; apostille or consular legalization may be required by the bank, notary, or compliance provider

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference, source-of-funds evidence, and source-of-wealth evidence where requested by the formation agent or financial institution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Regulated bank, auditor, employer, tax authority, or other independent evidentiary source
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Certified copy and, where issued abroad as a public document, Hague Apostille OR Consular Legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: French-language certified translations of foreign-language documents
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: French court-certified translator or translator accepted by the relevant French authority
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Certified translation; apostille or legalization of the underlying document remains separately applicable

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Before incorporation, onboarding, banking, and material ownership or management changes, screen all shareholders, directors, authorized signatories, beneficial owners, senior managers, and relevant counterparties against French and EU consolidated sanctions lists, the French national asset-freeze register maintained by the French Treasury, United Nations Security Council sanctions lists, and adverse-media databases. PEP screening must cover domestic and foreign PEPs, family members, and known close associates under Articles L.561-10 and R.561-18 et seq. of the Monetary and Financial Code, with enhanced due diligence, senior-management approval, source-of-wealth and source-of-funds verification, and enhanced ongoing monitoring. OFAC screening is not generally a standalone mandatory French-law requirement, but is required on a risk and nexus basis where there is a U.S. person, U.S. financial institution, U.S.-dollar clearing, U.S.-origin goods or technology, or contractual compliance obligation. No nominee, unexplained intermediary, opaque trust, bearer-share, or unexplained circular-ownership structure should be accepted.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: French Business Formalities One-Stop Shop (Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises): https://formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr/ ; technical registry and name-availability resources are operated through the Institut national de la propriété industrielle (INPI): https://data.inpi.fr/
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: A SARL name must be stated in the incorporation documents and must include or be accompanied by the legal-form designation Société à responsabilité limitée or SARL. France does not impose a general requirement that a company name be in French, but the name must be sufficiently distinctive, lawful, non-misleading, and compatible with public order. French registration accepts Latin-script names; non-Latin or transliterated names should be accompanied by a clear Latin transliteration for registry, banking, tax, customs, and contractual use. Name clearance does not replace trademark clearance, domain-name clearance, trade-name clearance, or review for unfair competition and parasitism.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Terms implying a regulated banking, credit, payment, insurance, investment-services, financial, or electronic-money activity without the relevant authorization, including banque, bank, crédit, credit, assurance, insurance, établissement de paiement, monnaie électronique, finance, investissement, and similar expressions

Terms implying a regulated legal, public, governmental, diplomatic, academic, medical, pharmaceutical, audit, accounting, architectural, or notarial status without legal entitlement, including avocat, notaire, expert-comptable, commissaire aux comptes, architecte, pharmacie, université, ministère, consulat, ambassade, République, and similar expressions

Protected public-service, national, territorial, or official designations, and names likely to create confusion with a public authority, regulated profession, existing company, trademark, or established trade name
Words suggesting an activity requiring authorization or licensing where the company has not obtained or cannot lawfully claim the relevant authorization
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: France has no general statutory 30-day company-name reservation mechanism comparable to jurisdictions that issue a formal name-reservation certificate. Conduct an INPI and RNE search, a trademark search through INPI, an EUIPO search, a domain-name search, and an adversarial trade-name search before filing. If the Guichet unique or registry rejects the name or related filing, obtain the written reason, correct or supplement the filing within the stated cure period, and resubmit electronically. For a formal administrative decision, file a reasoned internal administrative appeal with the issuing authority and, where appropriate, a judicial challenge within the applicable procedural period. A refusal or dispute concerning a commercial-register filing may also require an application to the competent French commercial court or its registry judge. A separate trademark objection or infringement issue must be handled under the applicable INPI, EUIPO, or court procedure. There is no automatic extension because no statutory name-reservation period exists.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A SARL must have a registered office in France and maintain a legally usable address capable of receiving official correspondence and supporting registry, tax, banking, and AML verification. A domiciliation company may be used if it is authorized under Articles L.123-11-1 et seq. of the French Commercial Code and the required domiciliation contract and supporting documents are maintained. A virtual office is generally acceptable for an online retailer of musical instruments and studio audio equipment at the incorporation stage, provided the activity is genuinely conducted from lawful premises and the provider permits the declared use. It is not sufficient where stock, employees, customer returns, warehousing, product testing, import operations, or regulated logistics are actually conducted elsewhere without disclosure. The bank, payment processor, customs authorities, tax administration, or AML provider may require evidence of real management, operating premises, contracts, inventory arrangements, and French or EU commercial substance.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: No official France-wide probability is published for unannounced inspections of newly incorporated online retailers. An indicative risk assessment for this low-risk, non-licensed activity is low, approximately 5-10 percent during the first 24 months absent red flags, increasing materially if there are VAT anomalies, repeated customs discrepancies, high-risk jurisdictions, sanctions alerts, unexplained payment flows, consumer complaints, product-safety issues, cash-intensive activity, or mismatch between the registered office and actual operations. This is an operational estimate, not a statutory probability or government statistic.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code (Code de commerce), Articles L.223-1 through L.223-43 (SARL); Article L.223-7 on articles of association; Article L.223-18 on day-to-day management by a gérant
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) operated by the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce, filed through the Guichet Unique (Business Formalities Centre)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form M0 (déclaration de constitution) and the formal application for registration on the Register of Commerce and Companies (immatriculation au RCS)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: French SARL has no legally fixed minimum share capital; the articles may set any amount. At formation, the total subscription must be fully paid up (in cash or in kind) and placed in a dedicated bank account or with a notary or escrow agent until registration is obtained; proof of payment is required in the registration file.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED FIRST: The Subscribers approve the draft Articles of Association of the Société à Responsabilité Limitée and each Subscriber accepts, subscribes for, and fully pays the shares set opposite his or her name in the subscription schedule. RESOLVED SECOND: The registered office is established at [address], France. RESOLVED THIRD: [Full name] is appointed as Gérant for an unlimited term, with full power to act on behalf of the company in all matters within the corporate purpose. RESOLVED FOURTH: All acts performed prior to this resolution in connection with incorporation are ratified and confirmed, and the Gérant is authorised to complete all formalities with the RCS and legal announcement publications.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Verify business name availability and corporate object compatibility
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INPI (Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle) via Infogreffe
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a search of the national trade mark register and the RCS database to ensure the proposed corporate name and principal activity are adheren to Article L.223-1 of the Commercial Code. No formal reservation is made; availability is confirmed by absence of conflicting prior rights.
required_dossiers: Identity of founders (passport or national identity card)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is unavailable or the object is too broad, the founders must revise the name or narrow the activity description and resubmit the search.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft and execute the Articles of Association (statuts)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Private notarial office or the founders themselves (statutory counsel not mandatory)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the articles containing the corporate name, registered office address, share capital, share ownership, management structure, and the detailed corporate object covering online retail of musical instruments and studio audio equipment (ISIC 4791). Each founder signs the articles. If assets are contributed, a valuation report may be required under Article L.223-9.
required_dossiers: Inventory of in-kind contributions and valuation report (if any)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the commercial court queries under-capitalisation or unclear object, the founders must amend the articles and re-execute the document.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Deposit and block the paid-up share capital in a dedicated bank account
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: French bank. Fiduciary (accredited financial institution) or notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary ‘funds to be blocked’ account in the name of the SARL in formation. Transfer the full subscribed capital. Request a certificate of deposit (attestation de dépôt de fonds) listing the shareholders and amounts.
required_dossiers: Bank certificate of deposit / notary deposit receipt
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank or notary refuses to issue the certificate, the founders must clear the identity and source-of-funds documentation and obtain a new certificate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Public notice of incorporation in a legal announcement journal
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Legal advertisement journal (Journal d'Annonces Légales, e.g. Les Affiches Parisiennes / Le Bulletin)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the incorporation notice containing the corporate name, legal form, capital amount, registered office, corporate object, and the identity of the gérant. Publish the notice in a court-approved legal announcements journal in the department where the registered office is located.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the publisher requires corrections due to incomplete information, the founders must revise and republish at their own cost.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submit the full registration file to the Guichet Unique / CFE
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Guichet Unique des Formalités des Entreprises (online portal operated by the French State)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the online M0 application, attach the signed articles, certificate of capital deposit, legal announcement certificate, power of attorney (if applicable), declaration of no criminal record for the gérant, and proof of power of the legal representative. Transmit the file electronically.
required_dossiers: Signed Articles of Association (original or electronic equivalent)
Certificate of publication in legal journal
Declaration of no conviction of the gérant
Power of attorney if an intermediary files
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Greffe issues a refusal or a query, the applicants must provide additional clarification, correct inconsistencies, or restate the corporate object; the file may be re-submitted after paying any additional fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Receive registration extracts, Kbis, and tax identifiers
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce / INSEE
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon successful validation, the Greffe registers the company in the RCS and issues an Extrait Kbis, SIREN, SIRET, and French VAT number (if required under EU VAT rules). The company is lawfully formed as of the date of registration.
required_dossiers: No further action needed by the company
Applicable identity verification for the gérant
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate or identifiers are delayed, the applicant may request acceleration from the Greffe or verify missing supporting documents.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable — pure online retail activity without industrial transformation or manufacturing of musical instruments or audio gear
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not required — no statutory operating licence for e-commerce retail; standard Kbis and business registration suffice

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Law on installations classées pour la protection de l'environnement (ICPE) — Direction régionale de l'environnement, de l'aménagement et du logement (DREAL)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt for standard warehouse storage of commercial finished goods below ICPE declaration thresholds; full EIA may be required only if warehousing area or storage volumes exceed prescribed limits
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial discharge applicable. For any warehouse space, maintain compliance with general waste handling obligations (Code de l'environnement, Articles L.541-21 et seq.), and limit noise, packaging waste, and light emissions to municipal and departmental urban planning standards.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: For the registered head office and any warehouse: workplace safety clearance under the Code du travail (electrical inspection, access, lighting, fire extinguishers), and fire safety compliance for business premises not open to the public. No ERP (établissement recevant du public) formalities apply to internet retail; a standard fire-safety certificate for offices/warehouses is sufficient.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) within the French Ministry of Economy and Finance; taxpayer and business-filing portal: impots.gouv.fr (Espace Professionnel); single company/ID formalities portal: formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr (Guichet Unique operated by INPI). Customs and export-clearance authority: Direction Générale des Douanes et Droits Indirects (DGDDI) via pro.douane.gouv.fr (DELTA electronic clearance).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a resident French SARL, statutory TIN/VAT IDs are issued through the Guichet Unique register portal: the incorporator files the M0 form together with the articles of association, registered-office evidence, and manager consent; upon INPI validation the SARL receives the 9-digit SIREN and 14-digit SIRET numbers, is entered in the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés, and obtains the Kbis extract. The DGFiP thereafter allocates the intra-Community VAT number (13 characters: FR + 2-digit key + 9-digit SIREN) without any separate VAT application, normally notified within 2-4 weeks through the company's professional tax space. A foreign entity without a French establishment that makes taxable supplies in France must register before its first French transaction with the SIE non-établi unit (dedicated VAT registration form) and receives a non-resident French VAT number that is not derived from a French SIREN; the OSS/IOSS regime remains optional for B2C distance sales.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation — the SARL is by default subject to Impôt sur les Sociétés (corporate income tax: 25% headline rate, 15% reduced rate on the first €42,500 of taxable profit for SMEs with turnover below €10m) at entity level, with no automatic pass-through to partners; profits and management results are taxed in the company, and distributions are separately taxed at the member level. Territorial_Scope: French branches of non-French corporate groups are taxed only on French-source taxable profits; the entity is not located in a Tax_Exempt_Zone, and Pass_Through_Eligible is not the default classification.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Check-the-box-type election available only under Art. 239 bis AB CGI: a small SARL (turnover below €10m, fewer than 50 employees, capital continuously held by natural persons) may elect pass-through taxation at the income-tax (IR) level for a maximum period of 5 fiscal years by the corporate tax return filing deadline; the election is irrevocable during its term and terminates on cessation of eligibility. Reverse election: IR-transparent SARL forms (e.g., SARL de famille) may opt irrevocably into entity-level IS pursuant to Art. 239 CGI. Hybrid-mismatch elections: none — France applies ATAD-2 anti-hybrid rules (Art. 212 bis CGI) compulsorily in priority-ordering fashion to deny double-deduction, deduction/non-inclusion, and imported-mismatch outcomes; no elective check-the-box for hybrid entity classification exists.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.transfer_pricing_and_aeoi_annex: The SARL must maintain contemporaneous transfer-pricing documentation (master file/local file) under Art. L.13 AA LPF if controlled transactions exceed €400m group turnover or €50m French turnover thresholds; cross-border payments to related parties require beneficial-ownership and substance analysis. The entity is automatically enrolled in AEOI/FATCA exchange through its SIREN registration and CRS self-certification on bank account opening; tax residence certificate is issued by the DGFiP SIE upon request.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: TVA — Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée (French VAT, implemented pursuant to EU Directive 2006/112/EC); a single national indirect tax with no departmental or municipal VAT layer; auxiliary reduced rates: 10.0%, 5.5%, and 2.1%; 0% or exemption applies to exports, intra-EU B2B dispatches, and certain international services.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Under the franchise en base de TVA small-business exemption, VAT registration may be avoided while annual turnover is below €85,000 (principal supplies of goods, including musical instruments and audio gear) or €37,500 (services) per calendar year, under the 2025 harmonized EU SME thresholds. Crossing €85,000 triggers mandatory VAT registration and VAT collection from the date of the exceeding transaction; a business may voluntarily register below the threshold to recover input VAT. Non-established EU sellers cross a €10,000 EU-wide annual distance-sales threshold before a French VAT registration obligation arises in France (OSS election available); non-EU sellers are registrable from their first French taxable sale.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory structured electronic invoicing applies to all B2B transactions under the French e-invoicing reform: receipt capability from 1 September 2026 for all VAT-registered businesses; issuance from 1 September 2026 for large/medium enterprises and from 1 September 2027 for small/very-small enterprises. Invoices must be transmitted through an accredited PDP (Plateforme de Dématérialisation Partenaire) or the public PPF using Factur-X/UBL structured syntax; the platform forwards and reports invoice data to DGFiP. France does not impose real-time fiscal stamping or continuous control clearance; enforcement is performed downstream by DGFiP on the aggregated e-invoice and e-reporting dataset (B2C and cross-border flows included). Exports additionally require electronic customs clearance via DELTA with the DAU/EAD declaration and an EORI number.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Claim the 0% (exonerated) VAT rate on sales of musical instruments and audio gear only if: (i) goods are physically dispatched or transported out of the European Union by the seller, its subcontractor, or the buyer acting for the seller, with physical exit completed within 3 months (90 days) of the supply, per Art. 262 ter I-1 CGI; (ii) documentary proof is assembled, comprising the certified customs export declaration (DAU/EAD through DELTA), transport documents (BL/AWB/CMR), commercial invoice, and bank settlement evidence; and (iii) no fraudulent re-importation or redelivery into the French market occurs. Intra-EU B2B dispatches to a customer holding a valid EU VAT number are likewise exempt under Art. 262 ter I-2, subject to the EC sales list (recapitulative statement) and digitized transport proof. Services directly linked to exported goods (loading, transport, warehousing, customs) qualify under Art. 262 ter II. Sales to foreign end consumers via the EU OSS/IOSS are taxed at the destination-state VAT rate and are not zero-rated.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Certified Customs Export Declaration (DAU/EAD) generated in the DELTA system and export-confirmed by DGDDI
Bill of Lading, Air Waybill, or CMR road consignment note evidencing physical removal of goods from the EU within 3 months
Commercial invoice stating the 0% TVA exonération (Art. 262 ter I CGI) applied to the export sale
Bank remittance or payment-settlement evidence from the foreign buyer (inward remittance certificate equivalent)
Intra-EU: EC Sales List (déclaration d'échanges de biens/recapitulative statement) and the customer's valid EU VAT registration number
EORI number registration confirmation and, where applicable, Incoterms-based transport contracts
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DGFiP VAT audit window: standard 3-year reassessment period (Art. L.176 LPF), extended to 6 years for deliberately concealed taxable activity, and to 10 years for fraudulent export chains (fausse exportation, TVA carrousel) involving third-party participation. On audit failure, zero-rating is revoked, input VAT deductions are clawed back with full reassessment, and penalties are assessed: 10% for simple negligence; 40% for deliberate under-declaration (mauvaise foi); 80% for manœuvres frauduleuses or abuse of rights; late-filing penalties of 10% plus 0.5% per month; and monthly late-payment interest of 0.2%. Criminal exposure under Art. 1741 CGI reaches up to 5 years' imprisonment and a €75,000 fine; customs smuggling penalties under Art. 414 of the Code des douanes impose a fine of 1 to 3 times the evaded duties, up to 3 years' imprisonment, and seizure of goods; the exporter may also face EORI suspension, VAT-registration withdrawal, and joint-and-several liability for orchestration of a fraudulent zero-rating chain. Note: statutory exchange-control repatriation deadlines no longer exist in French law, but DGFiP audit practice applies the 180-day settlement benchmark as corroborating documentary evidence for export zero-rating claims.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (Bank of France) and the French Treasury (Direction Générale du Trésor) under the authority of the Ministry of Economy, Finance and Recovery; the ACPR (Autorité de Contrôle Prudentiel et de Résolution) supervises banking and insurance entities.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France is a member of the Eurozone; the Euro (EUR) is fully convertible for both current and capital account transactions. There are no exchange controls on capital movements, profit remittances, or dividend distributions, subject to compliance with EU anti-money laundering (AML) and counter-terrorist financing (CTF) regulations. Profit remittance is unrestricted for SARLs, provided that statutory audits (if applicable) and tax clearance are completed. Non-resident shareholders may freely repatriate dividends after withholding tax (if any) under domestic law and tax treaties.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: France does not impose mandatory surrender of export proceeds. Exporters may retain foreign currency in authorized bank accounts, but must report all cross-border transactions to the Banque de France for balance-of-payments statistics (via the 'Réglementation des changes' reporting system). There is no statutory timeline for conversion; however, for tax and accounting purposes, foreign currency receivables must be revalued at year-end. No minimum conversion ratio applies.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium. France recognizes Electronic Money Institutions (EMIs) under the EU PSD2 directive, regulated by the ACPR. Cross-border EMIs (e.g., Revolut Business, Qonto, or N26) can open accounts for French SARLs, but they may have limitations on high-volume trade settlements and often require a local IBAN. Legal constraints include mandatory ACPR authorization for EMI activities, and EMIs cannot provide credit or hold client funds beyond e-money limits. For a low-risk retail business, EMIs are viable for operational liquidity but not for large capital injections or complex trade finance.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: French banks generally require at least one director (or a legal representative) to be physically present for the initial KYC interview, especially for non-resident shareholders. Remote onboarding is possible for certain banks (e.g., BNP Paribas, Société Générale) using video identification and electronic signatures, but the bank may still require a physical visit for the first account opening or for high-risk jurisdictions. For a French SARL with non-resident directors, a physical presence in France or a visit to a French consulate for notarized documents is often mandated. The bank's compliance team may waive physical presence if the company has a local registered agent and all documents are apostilled and translated.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership complexity (e.g., non-resident shareholders, multi-tier corporate structure)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a detailed corporate structure chart, certified copies of passports, proof of address, and a legal opinion from a French attorney confirming the ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) declaration under French law (Code Monétaire et Financier). Include a notarized power of attorney if a representative acts on behalf of the company.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk jurisdiction exposure (e.g., payments from tax havens or sanctioned countries)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a comprehensive transaction history, customer due diligence (CDD) files for all counterparties, and a risk assessment report. Include evidence of compliance with EU sanctions lists (e.g., OFAC, EU Consolidated List) and a written explanation of the business rationale for any cross-border payments.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unusual transaction patterns (e.g., large cash deposits or rapid in/out flows)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Maintain a detailed ledger of all transactions, invoices, and contracts. Provide a business plan and cash flow forecast. For large capital injections, include the source of funds (e.g., shareholder loan agreement, share subscription agreement) and proof of tax declaration (e.g., Form 2777 for capital contributions).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Incomplete corporate documentation (e.g., missing Kbis extract or statutory accounts)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit the official Kbis extract (less than 3 months old), the company's articles of association (statuts), and the list of directors (gérants). If the company is newly formed, provide the certificate of incorporation and proof of registration with the RCS (Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés).

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant wire transfer protocols: Use SWIFT MT103 for international transfers. For capital contributions from non-resident shareholders, the purpose code must be '1100' (Direct Investment) or '1110' (Equity Capital) under the French balance-of-payments classification. The bank will require a copy of the shareholder resolution, a capital increase agreement, and proof of the source of funds. For loans from shareholders, use purpose code '1200' (Loans) and provide a loan agreement. All inbound transfers must be reported to the Banque de France via the 'Réglementation des changes' system if they exceed €15,000 (per transaction or cumulative). Verification includes anti-money laundering checks and confirmation of the beneficial owner.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing rails for trade settlements: For supplier payments, use SWIFT MT103 (single payment) or MT202 (bank-to-bank) for high-value transactions. For documentary trade, use Commercial Letters of Credit (LC) via the bank's trade finance desk, typically with MT700/MT707 messages. For recurring payments to EU suppliers, SEPA Credit Transfer (SCT) is the standard rail. For non-EU suppliers, SWIFT is mandatory. The bank will require invoices, purchase orders, and proof of delivery (e.g., bill of lading) to comply with AML and sanctions screening. For high-value disbursements (>€50,000), the bank may request additional due diligence on the beneficiary.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: FX Forwards (plain vanilla) - permitted for hedging commercial exposures, with a maximum tenor of 12 months for SARLs without a dedicated treasury function.
FX Swaps (currency swaps) - permitted for converting EUR to foreign currency and back, subject to bank approval and underlying trade documentation.

Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) - technically permissible for currencies with restrictions, but not applicable for EUR as it is fully convertible; banks may offer NDFs for exotic currencies if the underlying trade involves such currencies.
Currency Options (European style) - permitted for hedging, but require a higher credit rating or collateral; not commonly used for small SARLs.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 15th of the 3rd month after fiscal year end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines up to 7,500 EUR; potential administrative sanctions and company strike-off

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Accounts Deposit at RCS Greffe
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Minimum fine 1,500 EUR; repeated non-compliance may result in administrative strike-off

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory statutory audit if CA > 800,000 EUR or total assets > 400,000 EUR

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: No annual UBO confirmation filing required; maintain beneficial owner register and update upon changes

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: 100-600 USD for registered office; 500-2,000 USD for professional registered agent service
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: 0-5,000 USD depending on audit thresholds (typically 2,000-4,000 USD)

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Reduced rate of 15% on first €42,000 of taxable profit for companies with turnover < €10 million; R&D tax credit (CIR) and innovation tax credit (CII) available.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 2065 (and annexes 2060-2069) filed electronically via the EFI (Électronique de Formulaires Informatisés) or GEDI portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For calendar year-end companies, the return must be filed by the second business day after May 1st. For non-calendar year-end, within 3 months of fiscal year-end.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Company identification (name, SIREN, address, legal form, fiscal year dates).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Provide French tax identification number (if any) and permanent establishment details if applicable.
Report only French-source income attributable to the French permanent establishment.
Indicate prior-year losses available for offset against current year profits.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax credits (e.g., CIR, CII, foreign tax credits).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim credits only if eligible under domestic law or tax treaty.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Withholding tax on distributed profits (if applicable).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Not applicable for the company itself; relevant for shareholders.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty of 10% of tax due, plus 0.5% per month of delay, and 5% for failure to file. Interest on late payment (0.2% per month) also applies.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% (reduced to 0% under EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive if holding ≥10% for 2 years; treaty rates may apply).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke treaty relief, submit a certificate of tax residence (TRC) from the foreign tax authority, and file Form 5000 (or 5001) with the French tax administration. The reduced rate is applied at source if the TRC is provided in advance; otherwise, a refund claim can be made.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: statutory 33.33% (reduced under treaties, e.g., 0% for EU if beneficial owner). Interest: statutory 30% (reduced under treaties, often 0% for EU).

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: 400,000,000 EUR (group consolidated turnover) for full Master File and Local File; simplified documentation required for turnover >50,000,000 EUR.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France does not have a specific Economic Substance Regulation (ESR), but requires substance for tax residency and applies anti-abuse rules (e.g., substance over form, GAAR).

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate understatement of income, false accounting, or concealment of French-source profits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Penalty of 80% of the evaded tax (for bad faith) or 100% (for abuse of law), plus interest at 0.2% per month.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be held jointly liable for corporate tax debts if they participated in the evasion; criminal penalties include imprisonment up to 5 years and fines up to €75,000.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Creating a French entity with no real economic activity, employees, or premises, solely to obtain tax benefits or avoid tax in another jurisdiction.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of treaty benefits, recharacterization of transactions, and imposition of 100% penalty for abuse of law (abus de droit).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face personal liability for unpaid taxes and penalties if they knowingly used the entity as a sham; travel bans and asset freezes possible.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to implement anti-money laundering controls, or using the company for money laundering or terrorist financing.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines up to €1 million for companies, plus criminal penalties for directors; suspension of business activities.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors can be personally fined up to €375,000 and imprisoned up to 5 years; civil restitution of illicit funds.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Setting intercompany prices that deviate from arm's length, shifting profits to low-tax jurisdictions without economic substance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Adjustment of taxable income, 40% penalty for lack of documentation, and interest; potential double taxation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be held personally liable for penalties if they knowingly approved non-compliant pricing; criminal charges for tax fraud if intentional.
